Hourly up to seven days, then daily, then weekly past forty-five — the resolution follows the range because 2,160 bars in a 560px box is a texture, not a chart. Volume per execution is the largest number of items any single node emitted: a webhook trigger emits one item while the fetch behind it emits five thousand, so neither end of the chain is a fair reading. Every bar carries its own figures on hover and the table under each chart carries them without.

An anomaly is a comparison against this workflow's own history — median and median-absolute-deviation over its last four weeks, not a threshold somebody guessed. Two guards stop it crying wolf: a percentage floor as well as a statistical one, and no judgement at all on a workflow whose normal day is under twenty items.

No baselines yet. An anomaly is a comparison against this workflow's own history, and none of these has seven complete days of it — so nothing here can honestly be called abnormal, including the things that are.

8Where the data goes

No node-level data has been collected for this workflow yet. Item counts come from data.resultData.runData, which n8n only returns on a single-execution request — the collector fetches those on a budget, newest and failed first, so a workflow collected for the first time may not have any until the next pass. If n8n has already pruned an execution's data, it never will.

9What went through

No dimensions are configured for this workflow, so nothing is counted beyond how many items moved. A dimension names one field on one node — the upload bucket, the lead source, the contact — and counts it. Find the fields it actually emits with npm run wf-fields -- <workflow id>, which prints names and shape and never a value.

10How much reached each stage, and when

No checkpoints are registered for this workflow, so there is nothing to count per stage. Add the n8n node names you care about — npm run wf-add -- <url> --checkpoint "Fetch from Cratio" --checkpoint "Meta CAPI" — and the next collection will start counting each one separately, by hour.
